recipes.name: Burek
ingredients_raw: salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

Cook and stir ground beef in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat until browned and crumbly, 5 to 7 minutes; drain fat. Stir in allspice, paprika, salt, and pepper. Transfer mixture to a large bowl and stir in potato and onion.

Stack two sheets phyllo dough on a work surface. Spoon 1/8 of the beef mixture down one long edge of the stack, then roll phyllo around filling into a tube. Coil the tube into a snail shape and place onto an ungreased baking sheet. Repeat to make seven more burek, placing finished coils up against one another to keep them from unrolling. Brush melted butter over the tops.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 20 to 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Burek
raw_recipe.description: Burek, an Eastern European treat that's often served at breakfast, features a savory beef and potato filling rolled in sheets of buttery phyllo dough.

review.reviewBody: This was very tasty. It was much milder/blander than I expected with the given seasonings. I accidentally undersalted since I had seasoned the ground beef but forgot to add more seasoning after adding the potatoes. It was slightly dry--I might moisten with a little broth next time. I used one small Yukon and one small sweet potato. I wonder about adding chopped spinach or peas or shredded carrots next time. Definitely worth trying again; I've never had this before but seems like it could be a good comfort food and is easy to make. I used too many sheets of phyllo so it wouldn't easily bend so I left it in long tubular rolls. I notice a 16 oz. box of phyllo contains 40 sheets (5 sheets per serving), so next time I would use that as a guide. I was confused and didn't intially realize that this should create 8 individual rolls, and perhaps only uses half of a 16 oz. pkg. of phyllo if only using 2 sheets per roll. I would think they could be shaped into a round spiral easier with fewer sheets of phyllo. I ended up with five long rolls. Definitely worth trying again. Kids and hubbie all ate and liked. We only ate about half of this so I would think it could easily serve 6 with a side dish. Thanks for sharing your recipe--I love trying new food combinations and the allspice really intrigued me. I might even add a little more allspice next time. And maybe minced apple. Hopefully fruit or other veggie additions would not completely destroy any ethnic authenticity.

This recipe is easy but not quite the MOIST burek I love so much! I think moisture is also the key to working with phyllo dough so here are a few ideas. 
1) Don't drain the beef too much - or at all! The grease helps to make the dough sheets pliable. 2) When you are not using the dough sheets cover them directly with a damp kitchen rag so they don't crack when you roll them up. 3) If the dough still isn't moist enough to work with you'll have to keep lathering on the butter as you roll it. Also I threw an egg in the beef mixture, which seemed to help. 

A little more grease may not make it healthier but it definitely makes it more delicious and more authentic!

For those people who are having trouble 'snaking' the filled pastry - change the wash you're putting onto the philo dough to 2Tbsp melted butter, 2Tbsp water, 3Tbsp Greek yoghurt and 1 large egg. Whisk together.

Also you'll need more layers of dough. I used 2 as the base > brush with egg wash > layer of dough > brush with egg wash > layer of dough > brush with egg wash > fill with meat filling, roll. Total of 4 sheets of dough per roll gives it a good bit more structure.

For traditional taste to it season only with salt and pepper. Phyllo sheets are hard to roll into rounds so you can have them simply straight. If you are able to make your own sheets as traditional burek has, dont brown the meat. Also, it has to be moistened to be moist. A cup or two of water, tbsp butter, and tsp of salt boiled together make huge difference. Ofc you lat it bake for 1-2 minutes more so there are no residues of butter-water.

My exchange student from Serbia enjoyed it very much! Added a small container of feta for added flavor and texture. Also cheated a little bit and used shredded hashbrowns. Will be adding drained cottage cheese tonight for a punch of additional protein. Thank you!

instead of using a whole tablespoon of allspice, i did a 1/2 tablespoon of allspice and a 1/2 tablespoon of veggeta instead. also, when i was mixing the beef/potatos/onions, i added a little bit of olive oil and water so it wouldnt be dry (but dont over-do it). i added enough water to where the meat and veggies would soak it up but in 5-10 minutes there wouldnt be any water left on the bottom. enjoyed the recipe it was awesome!

Made this for the first time tonight because I was trying to finish off some store bought philo pastry. Very thankful for all the comments. Helped me especially being new to handling philo sheets. I used A LOT of butter on each sheet and it made the spiral easy to form with the directed 2 sheet per Burek. I used garam masala seasoning because didn’t have all spice. I cut the potatoes into tiny cubes and cooked with meat and onions all together before I wrapped in pastry. Filling turned out nice. Having never eaten this before I wasn’t sure what to expect but I agree with some of the other comments that a dipping sauce of some kind to help with moisture. I can imagine sour cream or yogurt would punch it up. Otherwise, on its own it tasted nice. Thank you for the recipe.

I love burek and decided to try a different recipe. I really regret that decision and ended up throwing the whole pita in the trash due to the awful taste of the allspice. 
This recipe has way too much allspice and onion. Also, the complaints of dryness are because the meat shouldnt be cooked prior to baking. It should be rolled in the dough raw; it will cook in the oven.

My husband helped a coworker who is from Bosnia build a deck on his house. His wife prepared them a lunch of Berek and pickled veggies. I did some research and have tried to recreate berek and this recipe is really good. I don't know if its our American taste buds but I too thought it was a little bland. I made a spice mixture of garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, salt, pepper and a little dried oregano. I boiled the chopped potatoes for 5 minutes and added to the browned beef and onion with the spice mixture. I used 3 phyllo sheets per berek and brushed melted butter to seal. I tried the snail shape and it broke so I just rolled into a tube and put them next to each other. They were flaky and delicious. I made a spread of sour cream, dried dill and garlic powder. I love allrecipes.com because you can find a recipe that you have never tried to make before but can tweek it and make it your on that your friends and family love. Thanks, So GOOD!
Great recipe, my Croatian great Aunts would make this and I would watch as a child. Only difference they used pork instead of beef and added a mushroom sauce for it.

I make Burek but I make it in around 10 inch cake pan, I layer the phyllo dough then about half way I put in amixture of pork sausage and ground beef then layer it the rest of the way. My brother-inlaw is from Macedonia and this is how they make it. I think it looks like an apple pie.
Too much allspice; it overpowered the dish.
its amazing

Clear and concise recipe that is easy to follow. They taste great and can be reheated easily. The only thing I would ask of the author is suggestions for how to have this as a meal. What would it normally be served with other than the Balkan style yoghurt that is already suggested? Is it normally a standalone snack?

tried it for the first time with some friends from Montenegro. They loved it. The onion amount was not enough, I used an onion with a diameter of 2 1/2 inches. I would go with a larger one next time. Made some baklava for dessert with the extra filo dough... also great !

This was my first time making Burek and using phyllo dough, my Burek came out relatively good!! However I was making for a large family So I doubled everything in the recipe and all was well till I added two TBS of allspice, found out I hate how it tastes so next time I will use less allspice and I'm sure I will love it. I made a solace to dip the burek in out of sour cream, Dash table blend, dill weed and salt and pepper and it tastes very good on it. Great recipe overall! Jus taint overdo the allspice like I did ??

I was looking for a recipe to use up ground beef and phyllo dough and came across this. It was delicious as written, and wonderful to use as a base to build upon! Now, I had not used phyllo dough before, so I'm sure I messed that part of the recipe up, but even so it was delicious. Will make again.
I liked this recipe! It was easy.
I added a dash of ground clove. The aroma in my kitchen reminded me of being back in Bosnia.

I gave this 4 stars because it was very easy to make, and pretty good. A tad bit dry though, so it really needs someting to dip it in. Unfortunatly I did not have yogart, but it actually went well with some spicy mustard.
